dedupe_keys.name: contam multizone airflow and contaminant transport nist

description: CONTAM is NIST's multizone indoor air quality and ventilation program. It calculates airflows, including infiltration, exfiltration and room-to-room flows driven by fans, wind pressure and buoyancy; contaminant concentrations as they are carried by these flows and transformed by chemical and radiochemical reactions, sorption, filtration and deposition; and occupants' exposure for later risk assessment. Uses include checking the adequacy of ventilation, how ventilation varies over time and between zones, and relative pressures between zones. Version 3.4.0.1 is listed, last updated 8 January 2021; the ContamW interface runs on Windows and the ContamX engine on Windows and Linux, with related software on NIST's multizone modelling website and a user group. Coverage: generic. Access: free download. Licence: public domain; NIST calls the programs experimental and asks that derived works say so. Caveats: NIST calls the programs experimental, and results depend on how the building is divided into zones and airflow paths. Simulation uses: airborne infection, smoke and hazardous release scenarios, and ventilation design for hospitals and shelters. Related records: FDS and EnergyPlus.
